newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein higher, trade moderate.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein higher, trade moderate.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were higher in moderate trading on Tuesday as demand poured the market ahead of the weekend Eid al-Fitr celebration, traders said.
They said palm olein was traded at 1,450-55 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, higher than the previous levels of 1,445-50.
Crude palm oil was last sold on Saturday at an equivalent 1,270 rupiah/kg in a 1,000-tonne tender in Medan, north Sumatra.
"The market is quite active today because buyers are rushing to buy olein ahead of the Eid al-Fitr celebration," said one trader.
Traders said buyers made use of the remaining period before the celebration on February 9 and 10 to fill their stocks.
"Buyers have started buying so that their stocks will be enough for at least one week after the Eid al-Fitr," said another trader.
Traders said business usually slowed down after the celebration, mainly due to the fact that not so many truck drivers were available to transport goods.
They said tight supply and rises in Malaysia also boosted market sentiment, and added some buyers were still cautious because of last week riot in Rengasdengklok, West Java.

The data from Belawan also showed the MT Scapire had left for Port Klang in Malaysia with 9,700 tonnes of crude palm oil, while the MT Bunga Selasih had left for Pasir Gudang, also in Malaysia, with 10,500 tonnes of crude palm oil.
The data also showed that the MT Stokare will soon sail for Suez in Egypt with 700 tonnes of palm oil, while the MT Istana will leave for Semarang in Central Java with 2,000 tonnes of palm olein.
